newsitem.title: UK: ICCO raises 1995/96 cocoa surplus to 133,000 T.
newsitem.headline: ICCO raises 1995/96 cocoa surplus to 133,000 T.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) secretariat has revised up its forecast of the world cocoa surplus in 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) to 133,000 tonnes from a previous estimate of 120,000.

The total statistical stocks at the end of the last season should therefore increase to 1.404 million tonnes, which is equivalent to 51.7 percent or just above six months of projected annual world grindings, it said.
Total stocks directly overhanging the market, excluding the ICCO buffer stocks, would amount to 1.327 million tonnes, or about 5.5 months of estimated world grindings.

The ICCO revised up world production of cocoa beans by 146,000 tonnes to 2.877 million in 1995/96. Higher estimates were made for Ivory Coast, up 100,000 tonnes to 1.2 million, Ghana, up 25,000 tonnes to 400,000, Brazil, Ecuador and Cameroon. The estimate for Malaysia was lowered by 10,000 tonnes.
Grindings were revised up by 31,000 tonnes to 2.715 million tonnes with higher estimates seen for the UK, the Netherlands, Brazil, Canada and Japan.
Note - The ICCO secretariat revised its production figure for Ivory Coast to 1.2 million tonnes during a Council meeting in September.
The previous quarterly report had the Ivorian crop at 1.1 million tonnes.
